name: onebnpl-aics
description: ONE BNPL — AI-Powered Credit Scoring Model (AICS). Fintara Solutions Pvt Ltd.

scripts.build: npm run build -w @aics/contracts && npm run build -w @aics/api && npm run build -w @aics/web
scripts.test: npm run test -w @aics/contracts && npm run test -w @aics/api
scripts.lint: npm run lint -w @aics/api && npm run lint -w @aics/web
scripts.typecheck: npm run typecheck -w @aics/contracts && npm run typecheck -w @aics/api && npm run typecheck -w @aics/web

overridesRationale.postcss: Next bundles postcss 8.4.31, which is affected by three advisories (XSS via unescaped </style>, and arbitrary .map file disclosure via attacker-controlled sourceMappingURL). Fixed above 8.5.17. npm's suggested remediation was downgrading Next to v9, so we pin the patched patch-level release instead — postcss 8.5.x is API-compatible with 8.4.x.
overridesRationale.sharp: Next's image optimiser pulls sharp 0.34.5, which inherits four libvips CVEs (CVE-2026-33327/33328/35590/35591). Fixed in 0.35.0.

acceptedAuditExceptions.status: ACCEPTED — no viable fix at this time
acceptedAuditExceptions.rationale: The advisory range covers every release except 5.0.8, and 5.x is a breaking change: its CommonJS entry exports { expand } where minimatch@3 does `require('brace-expansion')` and invokes the result directly. Overriding to 5.x breaks eslint at load time. Impact is a denial of service triggered by a maliciously crafted glob pattern, reachable only by whoever already controls our lint/build invocation. Both consumers are devDependencies and are excluded from the production images, which install with --omit=dev.
acceptedAuditExceptions.revisit: When eslint and @nestjs/cli ship on a minimatch release that depends on brace-expansion >=5.0.8, drop this entry and upgrade.
